items.title: ICS Combiner
items.text:
ICS Combiner is a FastAPI service that merges multiple iCalendar (ICS) feeds into a single combined calendar, with optional per‑calendar transforms and PostgreSQL‑backed caching.

Use this documentation to:

  • Understand what the service does
  • Get started running it locally or via Docker
  • Configure environment variables and calendar sources
  • Explore the available HTTP endpoints and query parameters

items.title: cache
items.text:
Cache layer for ICS Combiner.

Cache is the facade the app uses. It serializes values as JSON, keeps hit/miss statistics, and never raises into the request path: backend errors are logged (rate limited), counted in CacheStats.errors, and turned into misses.

Backends: - PostgresBackend: a table in the service's own PostgreSQL database (DATABASE_URL). Connects lazily, backs off for 30 s after any database error, and creates its table on first use. - MemoryBackend: a process-local dict for local development and tests (CACHE_BACKEND=memory).

items.title: PostgresBackend
items.text:
PostgresBackend(conninfo: str, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic)

Cache table in PostgreSQL via a small sync connection pool.

Constructing it does no I/O. The pool opens on the first operation, the table is created once per process after the first successful connect, and any database error starts a 30 s backoff during which every operation is a miss and is_connected() is False (it never does I/O itself).

items.title: Configuration
items.text: ICS Combiner is configured via environment variables. These are typically set in an .env.local file for local development or Docker.

items.title: Core Settings
items.text:
• ICS_API_KEY – API key to enable path‑based authentication (optional for local/dev)
  • SALT – Optional salt used when computing the API path hash (preferred)
  • MD5_SALT – Legacy name for SALT (still supported)

items.title: Calendar Sources
items.text:
• ICS_SOURCES – JSON array of calendar configs. Each object may include:

  • Id (required, int): unique numeric ID per calendar

  • Url (required, string): ICS feed URL
  • Duration (optional, minutes): override event duration when DTSTART is datetime
  • PadStartMinutes (optional, minutes): prepend minutes and extend duration accordingly
  • Prefix (optional, string): prefix for SUMMARY
  • MakeUnique (optional, bool): force UID uniqueness per calendar
  • FilterDuplicates (optional, bool): de‑duplicate events by UID

  • RefreshSeconds (optional, int): cache TTL for this calendar’s source ICS Set to 0 to bypass the fresh source cache while still using failure backoff and last-known-good fallback cache when a cache is configured.

  • ICS_NAME – Combined calendar display name

  • ICS_DAYS_HISTORY – Days of history to include (int)

items.title: Cache
items.text:
The cache is optional. CACHE_BACKEND=memory selects a process-local cache; otherwise a set DATABASE_URL selects PostgreSQL; with neither, every request fetches the upstream feeds.

  • DATABASE_URL – PostgreSQL URL, e.g. postgresql://user:password@host:5432/ics_combiner?sslmode=require
  • CACHE_BACKEND – memory for a process-local cache (local development); takes precedence over DATABASE_URL

  • ICS_CACHE_NAMESPACE – Optional cache key namespace. Set this to a stable, unique value per app when several apps share one cache database. If omitted, a namespace is derived from ICS_API_KEY when available.

  • CACHE_TTL_ICS_SOURCE_DEFAULT – Default TTL (seconds) for source ICS caching (used when a source does not define RefreshSeconds)

  • CACHE_TTL_ICS_SOURCE_LKG – Optional last-known-good fallback TTL (seconds). Leave unset or set to 0 to retain indefinitely, which is the default.
  • CACHE_TTL_ICS_SOURCE_FAILURE_BACKOFF – Backoff TTL after a source fetch failure (seconds; default: 60; minimum: 1)
  • CACHE_TTL_ICS_SOURCE_RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF – Backoff TTL after HTTP 429 without Retry-After (seconds; default: 3600; minimum: 1)

When configured, ICS Combiner caches fetched ICS files to reduce load on upstream calendar providers. The PostgreSQL backend:

  • connects lazily on first use (startup never waits for the database);
  • creates its table, cache_entries, on first connect. It is a logged table, so last-known-good feeds and the sources index (stored with no expiry) survive a database crash or failover. The database user needs CREATE on schema public; if it lacks it, the service logs a warning naming the fix (GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO <user>, run as postgres);
  • never fails a request: after any database error it logs (at most once a minute per operation), fetches upstream directly for 30 seconds, then retries.

Cache keys are scoped by namespace so multiple apps can share the same cache database. The app also tracks source keys in that namespace and deletes cached primary/LKG entries for calendars removed from ICS_SOURCES on the next combine request.

items.title: Endpoints
items.text: ICS Combiner exposes a small set of HTTP endpoints for health checks and combined calendar retrieval.

items.title: Health
items.text: • GET /app/health – Returns basic health status (no authentication required).

items.title: Combined Calendar
items.text:
• GET /app/{ICS_API_KEY}/{hash}/ics

Returns the combined ICS calendar built from the configured ICS_SOURCES.

Query parameters:

  • show: optional comma‑separated list of calendar IDs to include (e.g. show=1,2).
  • hide: optional comma‑separated list of calendar IDs to exclude (e.g. hide=3).

Authentication:

  • ICS_API_KEY is the API key configured via environment variable.
  • hash is computed from ICS_API_KEY and optional SALT (or legacy MD5_SALT) using SHA‑256 (same scheme as the MCP servers).

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: This guide walks through running the ICS Combiner service locally and with Docker.

items.title: Run Locally
items.text:
1. Create and populate your environment file:
cp .env.example .env.local
# edit .env.local with your ICS sources, cache (DATABASE_URL), and auth settings
  1. Install dependencies:
pip install -e .
  1. Start the FastAPI app with Uvicorn:
python -m uvicorn src.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
  1. Check the health endpoint:
curl http://localhost:8080/app/health

items.title: Run Tests
items.text:
1. Install development dependencies:
pip install -e ".[dev]"
  1. Run the unit tests:
python -m pytest

items.title: Run with Docker
items.text:
1. Build the image:
docker build -t ics-combiner .
  1. Run the container:
docker run --env-file .env.local -p 8080:8080 ics-combiner
  1. Access endpoints via http://localhost:8080.
